The *Nandakattheraapadāna* (Tha Ap 408) is a verse narrative in the Therāpadāna section of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya recounting the past-life deeds and spiritual biography of the elder Nandaka. In an analysis of the distribution and chronology of Pali aorist forms, Paul Kingsbury identifies Apadāna 408 as exhibiting notable clustering or priming effects in verbal morphology, pointing out that seven of the nine canonical attestations of the thematic aorist *sannipatuṃ* occur in successive verses of this specific text [Kingsbury 2002].
